items.title: Filmography: Woody Allen
items.description:
Heywood Allen (born Allan Stewart Konigsberg; December 1, 1935) is an American filmmaker, actor, and comedian whose career spans eight decades (the 1950s to the 2020s). Allen began his career writing material for television in the 1950s, alongside Mel Brooks, Carl Reiner, Larry Gelbart, and Neil Simon. He also published several books of short stories and wrote humor pieces for The New Yorker. In the early 1960s, he performed as a stand-up comedian in Greenwich Village, where he developed a monologue style (rather than traditional jokes) and the persona of an insecure, intellectual, fretful nebbish.
  • What's New Pussycat (1965) [writer and actor]
    A playboy who refuses to give up his hedonistic lifestyle to settle down and marry his true love seeks help from a demented psychoanalyst who is having romantic problems of his own.
  • What's Up, Tiger Lily? (1966)
    Perhaps the first ever gag dub, one of the 1965 Japanese spy film Kokusai himitsu keisatsu: Kagi no kagi, turning it into a comedy about an agent pursuing the world's greatest egg salad recipe.
  • Casino Royale (1967) [actor only]
    After M's death, Sir James Bond is called out of retirement to stop SMERSH. In order to trick SMERSH and Le Chiffre, Bond thinks up the ultimate plan: every agent shall be dubbed James Bond. One Bond, real name Evelyn Tremble, is sent to take on Le Chiffre in a game of baccarat, but all of the Bonds get more than they can handle.
  • Take the Money and Run (1969)
    A mockumentary of inept petty criminal Virgil Starkwell.
  • Don't Drink the Water (1969) [writer only]
    Based on Allen's play of the same name, the Hollanders' European vacation is interrupted when their plane is forced to land in Vulgaria. The Hollanders leave the plane to take pictures which results in accusations of spying. Chased by soldiers, they take refuge in the American Embassy under the protection of the absent ambassador's hapless son.
  • Bananas (1971)
    A bumbling New Yorker is dumped by his activist girlfriend, so he travels to a tiny Latin American nation and becomes involved in its latest rebellion.
  • Play It Again, Sam (1972) [writer and actor]
    A Casablanca obsessed film critic seeks to get over his wife leaving him by dating again with the help of a married couple and his illusory idol, Humphrey Bogart.
  • Everything You Always Wanted to Know About Sex* (*But Were Afraid to Ask) (1972)
    Seven segments related to one another only in that they all purport to be based on sections of the book by David Reuben. The segments range from "Do Aphrodisiacs Work?" in which a court jester gives an aphrodisiac to the Queen and is, in the end, beheaded to "What Happens During Ejaculation?" in which we watch "control central" during a successful seduction.
  • Sleeper (1973)
    Nerdy health food store owner Miles is revived out of cryostasis 200 years into the future to fight an oppressive government.
  • Love and Death (1975)
    In czarist Russia, a neurotic soldier and his distant cousin formulate a plot to assassinate Napoleon.
  • The Front (1976) [actor only]
    In 1953, a cashier poses as a writer for blacklisted talents to submit their work through, but the surrounding injustice motivates him to take a stand.
  • Annie Hall (1977)
    A divorced Jewish comedian reflects on his relationship with his ex-lover, an aspiring nightclub singer, which ended abruptly just like his previous marriages.
  • Interiors (1978)
    Three sisters find their lives spiraling out of control in the wake of their parents' sudden, unexpected divorce.
  • Manhattan (1979)
    The life of a divorced television writer dating a teenage girl is further complicated when he becomes enamored with his best friend's mistress.
  • Stardust Memories (1980)
    While attending a retrospective of his work, a filmmaker recounts his life and loves: the inspirations for his films.
  • A Midsummer Night's Sex Comedy (1982)
    In the early 20th-century, wacky inventor Andrew Hobbs and his wife Adrian invite two other couples for a weekend party at their romantic summer house in the countryside.
  • Zelig (1983)
    A 'documentary' about a man who can look and act like whoever he's around, and encounters various famous people.
  • Broadway Danny Rose (1984)
    A hapless but devoted talent agent attempts to reconcile a lounge singer with his mistress.
  • The Purple Rose of Cairo (1985)
    A movie star exits the screen into 1935 New Jersey and the life of a waitress seeking an escape from her dreary surroundings.
  • Hannah and Her Sisters (1986)
    Between two Thanksgivings two years apart, Hannah's husband falls in love with her sister Lee, while her hypochondriac ex-husband rekindles his relationship with her sister Holly.
  • Radio Days (1987)
    A nostalgic look at radio's golden age focusing on one ordinary family and the various performers in the medium.
  • September (1987)
    At a Vermont summer house, Howard falls in love with Lane, who's in a relationship with Peter, who's falling for Stephanie, who's married with children.
  • Another Woman (1988)
    Facing a mid-life crisis, a college dean goes on sabbatical and rents an apartment next to a psychiatrist's office to write a new book, then is drawn to the plight of a pregnant woman seeking that doctor's help.
  • New York Stories (1989)
    A middle-aged artist obsessed with his pretty young assistant (dir. Martin Scorsese), a precocious 12-year-old living in a hotel (dir. Francis Ford Coppola), and a neurotic lawyer with a possessive mother make up three Gotham tales.
  • Crimes and Misdemeanors (1989)
    An ophthalmologist's mistress threatens to reveal their affair to his wife while a married documentary filmmaker is infatuated with another woman.
  • Alice (1990)
    A spoiled housewife reevaluates her life after visiting a Chinatown healer.
  • Shadows and Fog (1991)
    With a serial strangler on the loose, a bookkeeper wanders in search of the vigilante group intent on catching the killer.
  • Husbands and Wives (1992)
    When their best friends announce that they're separating, a professor and his wife discover the faults in their own marriage.
  • Manhattan Murder Mystery (1993)
    A middle-aged married couple suspect foul play when their neighbour's wife suddenly drops dead.
  • Bullets Over Broadway (1994)
    In 1928, a struggling playwright is forced to cast a mobster's talentless girlfriend in his latest drama in order to get it produced.
  • Don't Drink the Water (1994)
    Based on Allen's play of the same name (this TV adaptation is directed by him as well as the earlier iteration left Allen dissatisfied), the Hollanders' European vacation is interrupted when their plane is forced to land in Vulgaria. The Hollanders leave the plane to take pictures which results in accusations of spying. Chased by soldiers, they take refuge in the American Embassy under the protection of the absent ambassador's hapless son.
  • Mighty Aphrodite (1995)
    When he discovers his adopted son is a genius, a sportswriter seeks out the boy's birth mother: a ditzy porn star and prostitute.
  • Everyone Says I Love You (1996)
    A New York girl sets her father up with a beautiful woman in a troubled marriage while her stepsister gets engaged.
  • Deconstructing Harry (1997)
    Suffering from writer's block and eagerly awaiting his writing award, Harry Block remembers events from his past and scenes from his best-selling books as characters, real and fictional, come back to haunt him.
  • Celebrity (1998)
    The fortunes of a husband and wife differ drastically after they divorce.
  • Sweet and Lowdown (1999)
    In the 1930s, jazz guitarist Emmet Ray idolises Django Reinhardt, faces gangsters, and falls in love with a mute woman.
  • Small Time Crooks (2000)
    An incompetent crook and his wife strike it rich when a botched bank job's cover business becomes a spectacular success.
  • The Curse of the Jade Scorpion (2001)
    An insurance investigator and an efficiency expert who hate each other are both hypnotized by a crooked hypnotist with a jade scorpion into stealing jewels.
  • Hollywood Ending (2002)
    A director is forced to work with his ex-wife, who left him for the boss of the studio bankrolling his new film. But the night before the first day of shooting, he develops a case of psychosomatic blindness.
  • Anything Else (2003)
    An aspiring writer falls in love at first sight with a free-spirited, spontaneous young woman.
  • Melinda and Melinda (2004)
    Two alternating stories, one comedic, the other tragic, about Melinda's attempts to straighten out her life.
  • Match Point (2005)
    At a turning point in his life, a former tennis pro falls for an actress who happens to be dating his friend and soon-to-be brother-in-law.
  • Scoop (2006)
    An American journalism student in London scoops a big story, and begins an affair with an aristocrat as the incident unfurls.
  • Cassandra's Dream (2007)
    In dire straits, London brothers Terry and Ian, on their wealthy uncle's idea, turn to crime but things go awry and the two become enemies.
  • Vicky Cristina Barcelona (2008)
    Two friends on holiday in Spain become enamored with the same painter, unaware that his ex-wife, with whom he has a tempestuous relationship, is about to re-enter the picture.
  • Whatever Works (2009)
    A middle-aged, misanthropic NYC divorcé surprisingly enters a fulfilling, Pygmalion-type relationship with a much younger, unsophisticated Southern girl.
  • You Will Meet a Tall Dark Stranger (2010)
    As her own relationship begins to disintegrate, a young woman watches her parents' marriage dissolve when her father undergoes a mid-life crisis and impulsively weds a prostitute.
  • Midnight in Paris (2011)
    While on holiday in Paris with his fiancée's family, a nostalgic screenwriter finds himself mysteriously travelling back to the 1920s every day at midnight.
  • To Rome with Love (2012)
    Four tales unfold in the Eternal City: while vacationing in Rome, an architect encounters a young man whose romantic woes remind him of a painful incident from his own youth; a retired opera director discovers a mortician with an amazing voice, and he seizes the opportunity to rejuvenate his own flagging career; a young couple have separate romantic interludes; and a spotlight shines on an ordinary man.
  • Blue Jasmine (2013)
    A New York socialite, deeply troubled and in denial, arrives in San Francisco to impose upon her sister. She looks like a million bucks but isn't bringing money, peace or love.
  • Magic in the Moonlight (2014)
    In the 1920s, magician Stanley enjoys widespread acclaim as Chinese conjurer Wei Ling Soo, his stage persona. As arrogant as he is talented, Stanley despises claims by phony spiritualists that they can perform real magic. At the behest of his friend, Stanley travels to the Côte d'Azur mansion of the Catledge family to expose a young medium, but he's left surprised and shaken by evidence that her gifts may be real.
  • Irrational Man (2015)
    On a small-town college campus, a philosophy professor in existential crisis gives his life new purpose when he enters into a relationship with his student.
  • Café Society (2016)
    In the 1930s, a Bronx native moves to Hollywood and falls in love with a young woman who's seeing a married man.
  • Wonder Wheel (2017)
    In 1950s Coney Island, a lifeguard tells the story of a middle-aged carousel operator, his beleaguered wife and the visitor who turns their lives upside-down.
  • A Rainy Day in New York (2019)
    A young couple arrives in New York for a weekend, where they meet with bad weather and a series of adventures.
  • Rifkin's Festival (2020)
    A married American couple attends the San Sebastian Festival and get caught up in the magic of the event, the beauty and charm of the city, and the fantasy of movies.
  • Coup de chance (2023) [In French with embedded English subs]
    A young married woman runs into an old friend and is immediately smitten. The two friends grow increasingly close, eventually leading to infidelity and even a crime.

items.title: Flesh Gordon
items.description:
Flesh Gordon

Flesh Gordon est un film américain de science-fiction parodique et érotique réalisé par Howard Ziehm et Michael Benveniste, sorti en 1974.
Le film est une parodie érotique du serial des années 1930 ayant pour héros le personnage de bande dessinée Flash Gordon. Le film aurait été classé X par la Motion Picture Association of America (MPAA), mais fut remonté et amputé de certaines scènes pour obtenir un R ("R" pour restricted, interdit aux moins de 17 ans non accompagnés). Le film a été en compétition au Festival international du film fantastique d'Avoriaz 1975.
Une suite, Le Retour de Flesh Gordon finit par sortir en 1989.

L'histoire est familière pour celui qui a eu l'occasion de voir les Flash Gordon originaux, à ceci près qu'elle est épicée de kitsch et de sexe. Les noms des personnages sont sans grande finesse transformés pour leur donner une connotation sexuelle, à commencer par le nom du héros (flesh voulant dire « chair »), l'objet de sa lubricité est Dale Ardor (ardor, c'est-à-dire « ardeur » ; le personnage original s'appelle Dale Arden), et le maléfique empereur Wang le Perverti ("wang" étant une expression argotique désignant le pénis en Anglais). On trouve aussi un docteur Flexi Jerkoff (jerkoff désignant crument la masturbation) et Amora, la reine de la magie.
L'intrigue est la suivante : depuis son repaire de Porno, l'empereur Wang projette son « Sex Ray » en direction de la Terre, ce qui a pour épouvantable effet de transformer tous les habitants de la planète en obsédés sexuels. Seul Gordon peut remédier à la situation. En règle générale, tout est prétexte dans le film à montrer la nudité. Les scènes sont tournées quasiment de la même façon que le serial Flash Gordon originel, en noir et blanc. Un échantillon de l'humour des dialogues : la fusée spatiale vient juste de se poser sur la planète Porno. Une fois débarqués, Flesh et le docteur J aperçoivent au loin un dinosaure sauropode à long cou et à la tête ressemblant à un gland. Flesh demande au docteur J : « C'est quoi, ça ? », ce à quoi le docteur J répond : « Ça doit être une sorte de pénisaure. »
Mais, malgré une apparition relativement brève, la véritable vedette du film est un monstre gigantesque, à l'allure démoniaque, un monstre que l'empereur Wang sort de son hibernation et qui profère toutes sortes d'obscénités d'une voix voluptueuse qui jure avec son aspect monstrueux. Une illustration : tout en faisant un doigt d'honneur au personnage du titre, il se met à grommeler « Fourre-toi le, Gordon ! » Ce qui arrive à ce monstre constitue un élément majeur de l'intrigue.

Réalisateurs : Michael Benveniste et Howard Ziehm

Casting :
  • Jason Williams : Flesh Gordon
  • Suzanne Fields : Dale Ardor (Darlène en V.F.)
  • Joseph Hudgins : le professeur Flexi Jerkoff (Professeur Ejakul en V.F.)
  • William Dennis Hunt : l'empereur Wang le perverti
  • Candy Samples : Chief Nellie
  • Mycle Brandy : Amora, reine de la magie
  • John Hoyt : le professeur Gordon
  • Craig T. Nelson : le monstre (voix)
  • Lance Larsen : le prince Precious (Pédalo en V.F.)
  • Robert V. Greene : la voix du narrateur

From the Wikipedia entry for "Glorifying the American Girl":

"Glorifying the American Girl is a 1929 musical comedy film produced by Florenz Ziegfeld that highlights Ziegfeld Follies performers. The last third of the film (which was filmed in early Technicolor) is basically a Follies production, with cameo appearances by Rudy Vallee, Helen Morgan and Eddie Cantor.

The script for the film was written by J.P. McEvoy and Millard Webb and directed by John W. Harkrider and Millard Webb. The songs were written by Irving Berlin, Walter Donaldson, Rudolf Friml, James E. Hanley, Larry Spier and Dave Stamper. The film is in the public domain, and many prints exhibited on television are in black-and-white only, and do not include pre-Code material, such as nudity."

giving them the Inalienable Right to tell the rest of us

items.title: La Grande Vadrouille
items.description:
La Grande Vadrouille

Film franco-britannique
Réalisation : Gérard Oury assisté de Claude Clément
Scénario: Gérard Oury, Danièle Thompson, Marcel Jullian, d'après un premier scénario de Gérard Oury et Jean-Charles Tacchella

Genre : Comédie historique, Film de guerre
Date de sortie : 8 décembre 1966

En 1942, pendant l'Occupation, un bombardier britannique embarquant cinq hommes d'équipage est abattu au-dessus de Paris par la Flak, lors d'un retour de raid aérien. Ses occupants sautent en parachute. Deux sont faits prisonniers, les trois autres parviennent à échapper aux Allemands. Le premier, sir Reginald Brook (alias « Big Moustache »), atterrit dans le zoo de Vincennes, le second, Peter Cunningham, sur la nacelle d'un peintre en bâtiment, Augustin Bouvet, et le dernier, Alan MacIntosh, sur le toit de l'opéra Garnier avant de se réfugier dans la loge d'un chef d'orchestre acariâtre, Stanislas Lefort.
Bouvet et Lefort doivent alors, malgré eux, cacher les aviateurs avant de les aider à rejoindre la zone libre, et de là l'Angleterre. Pourchassés par les Allemands et notamment le major Achbach, les fugitifs traversent de nombreuses péripéties lors de leur voyage vers la Bourgogne. Ils franchiront enfin la fameuse « ligne de démarcation », avec l'aide de Germaine, la patronne de l'« hôtel du Globe » à Meursault, et atteindront la zone libre en planeur.

Casting :
  • Bourvil : Augustin Bouvet, peintre en bâtiment

items.title: Murder by Death
items.description:
Murder by Death is a 1976 American mystery comedy film with a cast featuring Eileen Brennan, Truman Capote, James Coco, Peter Falk, Alec Guinness, Elsa Lanchester, David Niven, Peter Sellers, Maggie Smith, Nancy Walker, and Estelle Winwood, written by Neil Simon and directed by Robert Moore.

The plot is a broad parody or spoof of the traditional country-house whodunit, familiar to mystery fiction fans of classics such as Agatha Christie's And Then There Were None. The cast is an ensemble of British and American actors playing send-ups of well-known fictional sleuths, including Hercule Poirot, Miss Marple, Charlie Chan, Nick and Nora Charles, and Sam Spade. It also features a rare acting performance by In Cold Blood author Truman Capote.

A group of five renowned detectives, each accompanied by a relative or associate, is invited to "dinner and a murder" by the mysterious Lionel Twain. Having lured his guests to his mansion managed by a blind butler named Jamessir Bensonmum, who is later joined by a deaf-mute cook named Yetta, Twain announces that it is in fact he who is the greatest detective in the world. items.title: Sabrina (1954)
items.description:
SABRINA ( Sabrina, 1954 - USA )
( Filme Completo / Legendado em Português )
Data de Lançamento: 22 de Setembro de 1954
»
SINOPSE:
Dois irmãos pertencem à uma poderosa família, sendo um deles (Humphrey Bogart) é um empresário incansável e o outro (William Holden) é um playboy incorrigível. Mas quando a filha do motorista (Audrey Hepburn) retorna de viagem, após passar dois anos em Paris, o playboy se modifica e, como ela sempre foi apaixonada por ele, tudo seria muito fácil de acontecer. Mas se os dois se casarem um poderosa fusão deve ser prejudicada, assim o irmão empresário decide intervir e também acaba se apaixonando por ela.
»
»
SOBRE O FILME:
Bem mais essencial que uma certa coerência nas decisões e sentimentos das personagens, o que em "Sabrina" às vezes se confunde, é a essência de um romance cômico que Wilder estabelece entre seus protagonistas e nosso romance por eles também. Há uma série de interesses subentendidos nas atitudes de Linus e Sabrina que variam com frequência, levando a uma quantidade de reviravoltas consideráveis nos minutos finais do filme e uma conclusão para alguns inimaginável. Entretanto, "Sabrina" acaba por ser um ótimo exemplo de como a criação de um universo e uma encenação que estabelece essas regras, de um mundo ingênuo apaixonado nesse caso, é bem mais importante que outros detalhes. 
.
Chega a me lembrar "The Big Sleep" do Hawks, também com o Bogart, que estabelece uma unidade definidora do que é um noir e isso acaba sendo o suficiente para um filme memorável, independente da trama ser toda mal resolvida. Em "Sabrina", a inicial inocência da personagem de Hepburn que mesmo se tornando mais madura permanece com as mesmas idealizações de antes traz uma leveza e um jogo de incertezas sobre o que decidirá fazer que é o mais essencial no que Wilder buscava contar. A elegância de Bogart e a imaturidade de Holden fecham esse triângulo amoroso que gira em torno da personagem principal. 
»
»

items.title: Scarlet Street
items.description: German director Fritz Lang is best known for the highly influential films from relatively early in his career, especially Metropolis (1927) and M (1931). But he also had a brief Hollywood heyday during the mid 1940s, when he made some of his best films. Scarlet Street has been claimed by film noir. This attribution is understandable. The lighting is dark, with heavy use of shadows. The characters are all shady as well. Kitty is certainly a femme fatale, although hints are dropped that she is an inherently decent person who has become completely corrupted by Johnny. Being the most naive, Robinson is also the most sympathetic. But even he eventually turns to crime to fulfill his passions. But while Scarlet Street has elements of film noir, it is in reality a black comedy. While Robinson plays it straight throughout, Bennett and Duryea camp it up marvelously. Bennett laughs when Robinson claims to be a painter: "And here I had you pegged as a cashier!" She also has to suppress laughter when Robinson reveals that he is married, and shock when Duryea passes her off as the mysterious painter.

items.title: SuperMarioLogan (SML) Archive
items.description:
UPDATE, June 12th 2022: Added a missing video, the last one they posted on the channel called "This channel will be deleted tomorrow". Thanks go to an IA reviewer for bringing the missing vid to my attention.

Also, I know IA isn't YouTube and I didn't make the content posted here, but thanks to everyone for 12K views. It's great to know that people really care about the content being preserved here and that it was worth the effort to protect it.

-------------------------------------------------------------


With official word that SuperMarioLogan will be deleting their original channel soon, I've decided to upload this archive for preservation's sake.

Like SML or hate it, the show's been around for many years and it's amassed tens of thousands of fans. The crass and deliberately shocking nature of its comedy makes SML controversial but I don't see it as meaningfully different from existing media like South Park.

One way or another it's a noteworthy piece of internet media that deserves to be preserved.


Other channels the SML project uploaded to are also archived

items.title: Tampopo (1985)
items.description:
The tale of an eccentric band of culinary ronin who guide the widow of a noodle-shop owner on her quest for the perfect recipe, this rapturous “ramen western” by Japanese director Juzo Itami is an entertaining, genre-bending adventure underpinned by a deft satire of the way social conventions distort the most natural of human urges—our appetites. Interspersing the efforts of Tampopo (Nobuko Miyamoto) and friends to make her café a success with the erotic exploits of a gastronome gangster and glimpses of food culture both high and low, the sweet, sexy, and surreal Tampopo is a lavishly inclusive paean to the sensual joys of nourishment, and one of the most mouthwatering examples of food on film ever made.

items.title: The Benny Hill Show
items.description:
The Benny Hill Show

- The alternative comedian Ben Elton made a headline-grabbing allegation, both on the TV show Saturday Live and in the pages of Q magazine (in its January 1987 issue), that The Benny Hill Show incited crimes and misdemeanours. "We know in Britain, women can't even walk safe in a park anymore. That, for me, is worrying." 
- A spokesman for the Broadcasting Standards Authority commented that "the convention is becoming increasingly offensive [...] It's not as funny as it was to have half-naked girls chased across the screen by a dirty old man."
- John Howard Davies, the head of Light Entertainment at Thames Television, was cited by the British press as the man who sacked Benny Hill when the company decided not to renew Hill's contract. "The show was past its sell-by date", Davies told The Guardian newspaper. "Benny was all right when he was young, but when you're in your 60s, it's a slightly different matter to leer at a pretty girl."
  source

- Recently, actress Debbie Arnold accused The Benny Hill Show of being “sexist”, "ridiculous" and “terrible” when she appeared on Good Morning Britain. "I mean, looking up girls' skirts, how can that be right for people to see that today?”
  source

- As the show became more and more out of touch, audiences plummeted [citation needed] until it was finally cancelled by ITV in 1989 - here are four jokes deemed horrendous by today’s standards:
  “Girls are like pianos. When they’re not upright, they’re grand.”
  “I’m not against half naked girls – not as often as I’d like to be.”
  “Roses are reddish, violets are bluish. If it weren't for Christmas, we'd all be Jewish.”
  “Did you hear about the actress who was so dumb, she couldn’t count to two without taking off her blouse?”
  source

items.title: The Flying Deuces
items.description:
This was the first comedy that Laurel and Hardy starred in without producer Hal Roach, although they had previously been "guest stars" in four MGM movies. 
After they finished making "The Flying Deuces," they returned to Hal Roach Studios to make films.

In order to make this movie, producer Boris Morros bought the rights to the 1931 French film "Les deux legionnaires," which had a similar plot. "The Flying Deuces" was Morros' first independent production and it was shot in continuity over a span of four weeks. 
Only one day was reportedly needed for retakes. 
The French original starred Fernandel and Noel Noel.

SYNOPSIS:
Ollie is in love with a woman. When he find out that she is already married, he tries to kill himself. Of course, the suicide is prevented and the boys join the Foreign Legion to get away from their troubles. Eventually, they are arrested for trying to desert the Legion and escape the firing squad by stealing a plane.

items.description:
http://www.imdb.com/title/tt0021890/
There's nothing like an original !!!
Hildy Johnson (Pat O'Brien), newspaper reporter, is engaged to Peggy Grant and planning to move to New York for a higher paying advertising job. The court press room is full of lame reporters who invent stories as much as write them. All are waiting to cover the hanging of Earl Williams. When Williams escapes from the inept Sheriff, Hildy seizes the opportunity by using his $260 honeymoon money to payoff an insider and get the scoop on the escape. However, Walter Burns (Adolphe Menjou), the Post's editor, is slow to repay Hildy back, hoping that he will stay on the story. Getting a major scoop looks possible when Hildy stumbles onto the bewildered escapee and hides him in a roll-top desk in the press room. Burns shows up to help. Can they keep Williams' whereabouts secret long enough to get the scoop, especially with the Sheriff and other reporters hovering around?
Nominated for three Oscars

items.title: The Pink Panther Cartoon Collection
items.description:
The animated Pink Panther character's initial appearance in the live action film's title sequence, directed by Friz Freleng, was such a success with audiences and United Artists that the studio signed Freleng and his DePatie–Freleng Enterprises studio to a multi-year contract for a series of Pink Panther theatrical cartoon shorts. The first entry in the series, 1964's The Pink Phink, featured Pink harassing his foil, a little white mustachioed man who is often considered a caricature of Friz Freleng (this character is officially known as The Little Man[2]), by constantly trying to paint the Little Man's blue house pink. The Pink Phink won the 1964 Academy Award for Animated Short Film, and subsequent shorts in the series, usually featuring the Pink Panther opposite the Little Man, were successful releases.

In an early series of Pink Panther animated cartoons, Pink generally remained silent, speaking only in two theatrical shorts, Sink Pink (one line) and Pink Ice (throughout the film). Rich Little provided Pink's voice in these shorts, modeling it on that of David Niven (who had portrayed Clouseau's jewel thief nemesis in the original live-action film). Years later, Little would overdub Niven's voice for Trail of the Pink Panther and Curse of the Pink Panther, due to Niven's ill health. All of the animated Pink Panther shorts utilized the distinctive jazzy theme music composed by Henry Mancini for the 1963 feature film, with additional scores composed by Walter Greene or William Lava.[
items.creator: Official Pink Panther

items.title: The Private Life of Don Juan
items.description:
In his last film role, Douglas Fairbanks as an ageing legendary lady-killer Don Juan.
It is set in Seville, Spain in centuries past, where once a young Don Juan caused ladies to swoon and jealous husbands to challenge him to a duel. 
After 20 years absence, he returns as a middle-aged married man feeling trapped by marriage and tempted to re-visit his old haunts. 
As it often happens with legends, however, the Don Juan of the past has become far greater and more wonderful in women's minds than he ever was, especially when a young imitator is killed (by a jealous husband) and mistaken for Don Juan. 
Then a book entitled 'the Private Life of Don Juan' is published and read by swooning women, and the whole thing is reminiscent of our real larger-than-life legends such as Elvis. And as with Elvis, whom we prefer to remember as young, slim and handsome, so Don Juan lives in women's minds so that the real middle-aged Don Juan is treated like a kindly father-figure by young women - much to his dismay!

items.title: Thunder in the City
items.description:
In this satire of British-American relations, Edward G. Robinson stars as Dan Armstrong, a hard-sell American salesman whose company sends him to England to learn how to tone down his act. 
There he meets some distant relatives, the aristocrats Sir Peter and Lady Challoner (Arthur Wontner and Annie Esmond). 
They invite him to their mansion for the weekend, where among the house guests are the penniless aristocrats the Duke and Duchess of Glenavon (Nigel Bruce and Constance Collier ) and their daughter Lady Patricia (Luli Deste), as well as a conniving stockbroker, Henry Graham Manningdale (Ralph Richardson). 
The Duke and Duchess own only an apparently worthless mine in Rhodesia that supposedly contains a metal called magnelite. 
Manningdale says that he will develop the mine in exchange for permission to marry Lady Patricia. 
Armstrong also has designs on Patricia, however, and he engineers a scheme to start a company and sell stock in the mine.

items.title: Trapeze Disrobing Act (Standard 4:3)
items.description: Camera is positioned as if in the audience at a vaudeville or burlesque show. Two men with long hair and beards in rough clothing appear to be eating and talking in a box on the left as a female aerialist sits on a trapeze over the stage and its painted backdrop of trees. Fully dressed in street clothing, the trapezist removes her jacket and hat before performing a flip. She stands to remove her skirt and then sits back down on the bar as she takes off her corset and throws it to the country bumpkins in the box, who fight over the undergarment. The trapezist continues to disrobe, removing her shoes, stockings, and garters, again throwing the latter to the men, and then seemingly hangs upside down (with her feet anchored off-camera) as she slips off her petticoat. Thus clad only in tights, trunks, and a camisole, the woman performs her trapeze act to the increasingly excited men. - From the Library Of Congress description
items.creator: Thomas Edison

Mike and Mousey (George E. Stone), a little chiseler who has attached himself to Mike, follow a clue to a small town.

items.title: Wide Open Marriage, Hausfrauen Report 4 1973
items.description:
A German "report" film, this time about Housewives. There were also report films done about husbands and most famously schoolgirls. This one passes on the "man in the street" interviews and just sticks to vignettes of various housewives finding entertainment while their husbands work. Sadly I could not find subtitles, though I think that does little to detract from the viewing experience. 

Rosi Mayr is in the film of course. She was in nearly all of the German sex comedies. Rosi started her film career at about 54 years of age and would go on to play bit parts in 131 movies but was a singer and stage actor before that. 

German language

items.title: (VHS) Toonami/Cartoon Network for August 11, 2013
items.description:
Thanks for watching!

Warning: THERE ARE A LOT OF VIDEO GLITCHES!!!

Advice: Just let the file play in real-time. It’s about ten hours long!

If you like any of the shows here, please consider buying the actual DVDs, VHS tapes, LaserDiscs, digital downloads, or streaming subscriptions to support the creators.

It took over three days to encode this, and blame Handbrake for the video glitches, not Lightworks, not iMovie, not Panasonic. Handbrake. There wasn't any other way to get this digitized.

Be grateful that this was even recorded at all by me. Apparently on a tape that has UPN’s Disney’s One Too, so an older, more rare children’s block was taped over just so I could watch Toonami and Cartoon Network later. (Ah, the old, awful way of constantly reusing video tapes.) Also, please don’t ask, nor make requests, for programming. Anything I upload is from my own personal collection of recordings. If I upload somebody else’s stuff, it won’t be branded with our watermark. If you want to help, consider, please, becoming a monthly patron at our Patreon: patreon.com/coffee4binky and please, enjoy the video.

In the 1930s, the series began to feature current popular musical guest stars such as the Mills Brothers, Rudy Vallee and Ethel Merman. In the 1950s, the series was syndicated to television by UM&M/National Telefilm Associates.

items.title: Aladdin (Mel-O-Toons)
items.description:
Mel-O-Toons sometimes erroneously called "Mello Toons", was a series of animated cartoons produced in 1960 by New World Productions and syndicated by United Artists. It featured various folk tales, Greco-Roman myths, Biblical stories, some original stories by author Thornton Burgess, classic stories, even adaptations of classical music and ballet. The soundtracks were often taken from existing children's records, licensed from the original labels. 104 cartoons, each about 6 minutes long, were produced in limited animation.

items.description:
CONTENT WARNING: The cartoons shown in this collection are products of their time. Some of these shorts depict some of the ethnic and racial prejudices that were commonplace in American society at their times. These depictions are wrong then and are wrong now. The cartoons here are presented in their unaltered forms. Due to some of the content depicted, some of these shorts are not suitable for younger viewers.

This is a collection containing all Looney Tunes and Merrie Melodies cartoon shorts which have fallen in the public domain, meaning that they are free to use and distribute. Many of these shorts fell into the public domain after United Artists (the copyright holder of the pre-1948 Looney Tunes and Merrie Melodies shorts) failed to renew the copyright for those shorts. Extra notes:

For the majority of the black and white Porky Pig and Daffy Duck cartoons which fell into the public domain, unofficial home video releases containing public domain cartoons featured the redrawn and colorized versions from the 1960's as opposed to the black and white originals, presumably because the prints were easier to find for the colorized versions at the time.

In the 1970’s, several black and white Looney Tunes and Merrie Melodies shorts were later redrawn and colorized without Warner Bros.’ involvement by a company named Radio and Television Packagers, who replaced the cartoons’ original soundtracks with a new soundtrack, and also gave some of the cartoons new titles (ex: “One More Time” (1931) was renamed “On Duty”). This was because all the shorts that were chosen for selection had fallen into the public domain by that point due to failure to renew the copyrights for those shorts. These versions can often be seen on low budget, unofficial home video releases containing public domain cartoons.

Three public domain cartoons are part of the "Censored Eleven", a series of eleven shorts banned from being officially released or aired on American television due to their outdated depictions of African Americans. These three shorts are "Hittin' the Trail for Hallelujah Land" (1931), "Jungle Jitters" (1938), and "All This and Rabbit Stew" (1941). Additionally, "All This and Rabbit Stew" is the only Censored Eleven short to feature Bugs Bunny, also marking it one of several Bugs Bunny cartoons to be banned from airing on American television for the same reason.

All shorts made between 1929 and 1931 are all in the public domain, as are the majority of the shorts made in 1932. The most recent short to fall in the public domain to date is "Puss N' Booty" (1943), which was the last short made in 1943 and the last Looney Tunes black and white short. As of now, all shorts made in 1944 and onwards are currently under copyright by Warner Bros.


All shorts were originally made by Warner Bros., but are all now in the public domain.

items.title: All public domain Popeye the Sailor shorts
items.description:
This is a complete collection of all Popeye the Sailor cartoons which have fallen into the public domain, meaning that they are free to use and distribute. Many of these shorts were made in the 1950's, when Famous Studios produced the series, although several black and white Popeye shorts produced by Fleischer Studios also fell into public domain. Additionally, all three of the Popeye Color Features made by Fleischer Studios have fallen into the public domain. For a long time until 2004, these shorts were the only ones to be released onto home video because of their public domain status. This was due to an ongoing dispute between King Features Syndicate (the copyright owners of Popeye and the comics he originated from) and United Artists (who owned the copyrights to the Popeye shorts at the time) regarding who was the true copyright owner of the shorts in terms of releasing them officially to home video.

The print which the Library of Congress has of this short can be viewed on their YouTube channel: Popeye the Sailor Meets Sindbad the Sailor - YouTube

Several of the black and white Popeye shorts, including those in public domain, were later colorized in the 1980's through redrawing every other frame of the shorts and adding color to them. These versions were commissioned by Ted Turner for airing on Cartoon Network.

items.title: All public domain Walt Disney Studios cartoons
items.description:
This is a complete collection of all cartoon shorts made by Walt Disney Studios after 1928 which have fallen in the public domain, meaning that they are free to use and distribute. Many of the shorts which have fallen in the public domain were originally made for the governments of the United States and Canada to encourage viewers to support the war. These shorts include Education for Death (1943), which described the horrible conditions of Nazi Germany during World War II, and The Spirit of  '43 (1943), which is noteworthy for being one of the few shorts starring Donald Duck to fall into the public domain.

A couple noteworthy shorts which do not fall under the WWII category include The Mad Doctor (1933) (one of very few shorts starring Mickey Mouse to fall in the public domain), Susie the Little Blue Coupe (1952), The Cookie Carnival (1935), and Hooked Bear (1956), among a few others. 

Most notably, Steamboat Willie (1928), the first cartoon to feature Mickey Mouse and the first cartoon to utilize sound, entered the public domain in the United States on January 1st, 2024. While it was public domain in the rest of the world for much longer, it was still under copyright in the United States up until that date due to several lawsuits brought on by Disney relating to the subject of extending the copyright of that particular short.

Here is a list of all the shorts which have fallen into the public domain:

Steamboat Willie (1928) - first cartoon short to utilize sound, first Mickey Mouse cartoon, preserved at the National Film Registry in the Library of Congress

The Gallopin' Gaucho (1928) - later digitally colorized through computers for television

Plane Crazy (1928) - released as both sound and silent versions

Minnie's Yoo Hoo (1930)

The Mad Doctor (1933) - later digitally colorized through computers for television

The Cookie Carnival (1935)

The Thrifty Pig (1941)

All Together (1942)

Out of the Frying Pan Into the Firing Line (1942)

Donald's Decision (1942)

The Spirit of '43 (1943)

Education for Death (1943)

The Winged Scourge (1943)

Cleanliness Brings Health (1945)

Susie the Little Blue Coupe (1952)

Hooked Bear (1956)


Extra notes:
Steamboat Willie (1928), the first Mickey Mouse cartoon and the first cartoon to utilize sound, had an odd copyright status in the United States up until 2024. While the short was in the public domain in the rest of the world, it was under copyright in the United States until 2024 due to several lawsuits brought on by Disney relating to the subject of extending the copyright of that particular short. On January 1st, 2024, the short fully entered the public domain, as did the version of Mickey Mouse seen in that short.

items.description:
All 40 episodes of DiC's single-season show "Archie's Weird Mysteries," obtained from the 4-disc DVD set. This set has been out of print since at least 2017, possibly 2012. Seemingly due to the recent Riverdale & Sabrina-influenced Archie boom, these DVDs list for between $50-450 on the secondary market. These are HEVC encodes I derived in HandBrake from a torrent. Some interlacing/banding seems endemic to the DVD that could not be removed.

Developed jointly by DiC in Burbank & their French subsidiary "Les Studios Tex" (itself named after American animator Tex Avery), the show complied with FCC educational programming guidelines. It was stationed on the quasi-education-focused "PAX" network, now known as "Ion," from October of 1999 to February of 2000. It has subsequently aired in syndication on several networks in the ensuing decades, with large lapses in availability. These files are hosted here for purely archival purposes at no gain.

items.title: Batman: The Animated Series - Full Series
items.description: Batman: The Animated Series (Often shortened as Batman TAS or BTAS is an American superhero animated television series based on the DC Comics superhero Batman. Dveloped by Bruce Timm and Eric Radomski, and produced by Warner Bros. Animation, it originally aired on Fox Kids from September 5, 1992 to September 15, 1995 with a total of 85 episodes. After the series ended its original run, a follow-up titled The New Batman Adventures began airing on Kids' WB in 1997 as a continuation of the series, featuring a revamped animation style. Lasting 24 episodes, it has often been included in the same syndicated re-run packages and home media releases. The New Batman Adventures is included. items.title: Beast Wars: Transformers (Complete TV Series, Seasons 1-3) [1080p AI Upscale]
items.description:
This upload compiles the complete run of the Emmy-winning Mainframe Entertainment/Hasbro venture "Beast Wars: Transformers" just in time for the series' 25th anniversary. All 3 seasons have been upscaled with AI to a sharp 1080p by reddit's u/Straken1 ("Al's" on YouTube), also viewable collected in their native playlist here. The results are very impressive, no doubt at least in part due to the crisp/flat early CG rendering inherent to the source material— it was TV's second-ever fully 3D animated cartoon, made by the same people behind "Reboot" (the first-ever).

I did not create the original series, nor this remastered version; I simply mirror the files here for archival purposes. The files, mostly .mkv with some .mp4, were obtained through youtube-dlg & remain unmodified other than slight renaming for organization.

items.title: Bugs Bunny - All This and Rabbit Stew
items.description:
All This and Rabbit Stew is a one-reel animated cartoon short subject in the Merrie Melodies series, produced in Technicolor and released to theatres on September 20, 1941 by Warner Bros. and Vitaphone. It was produced by Leon Schlesinger and directed by an uncredited Tex Avery, with musical supervision by Carl W. Stalling

The cartoon was the final Avery-directed Bugs Bunny short to be released. Although it was produced before The Heckling Hare (after the production of which Avery was suspended from the Schlesinger studio and defected to Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer), it was released afterwards. The title is a parody of that of All This and Heaven Too. Because the cartoon was released after Avery left Warner Bros., Avery's name does not appear in the credits.[1][2][3][4][5]

After copyright on All This and Rabbit Stew expired in 1969, the film fell into the public domain. The cartoon has been considered highly controversial due to racial stereotyping, which prompted United Artists to withhold this cartoon from syndication a year before it entered the public domain, making it one of the infamous Censored Eleven. The plot has Bugs Bunny hunted by a slow-witted African American hunter who sounds and looks like Stepin Fetchit. (Description source: Wikipedia, CC BY-SA)

Video from https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CgNjXeU5OTk

items.title: Cartoon Network "City"-Era Bumps 2004-2007 [Production Quality]
items.description:
This upload reflects ~250 different commercial bumpers produced for Cartoon Network by Australian VFX powerhouse Animal Logic. The files were obtained in the highest possible quality from the Vimeo account of geoffvster (Animal Logic animation supervisor Geoff Valent), often still including the production slate, timecodes, etc. Most of these were rendered at a stage in the production process wherein the sound was still in flux; many have voice acting but may or may not include sound effects & music is largely absent. The generally nondescriptive production names of the files are unaltered.

These bumps are fondly remembered for the slice-of-life view they provided of interactions between various Cartoon Network characters from different eras, such as Fred Jones of Scooby-Doo! chatting it up with the cast of Megas XLR in their mech at a stoplight. The enticing pervasive illusion of the network as a living, breathing place where cartoon characters resided & spent time in each other's company while going about their lives preceded similar concepts such as Space Jam 2's "Metaverse" (which as a fellow Warner Bros. product included many of the same characters, albeit in brief cameos generally without voice acting or any meaningfully apparent personality). At one point in time according to Valent the bumps were pitched to be adapted as an independent television program, but this never materialized for unclear reasons.

Several hundred bumps are thought to exist, making this page in the wider scope of things a relatively poor representation of the era. This defunct & unfortunately non-archived Kametsu thread allegedly contained a veritable trove of 616+ bumpers, many of which were geoffvster's high-quality uploads remuxed with finished audio as-aired. If you have these removed bumpers or other high-quality sources of bumps not archived here, please contact me.

These videos are presented for historical purposes only, being (like most old advertisements) unavailable for any sort of streaming or purchase. These interstitials have been off the air totally in the network's home country since 2007 with other territories dropping the bumps at different times; at the latest they ceased airing in Latin America circa 2010. Neither myself nor the Internet Archive benefit materially in any way from these uploads.

items.title: Cartoon Tape - Boomerang, Cartoon Network, Kids WB
items.description:
This excerpt consists mainly of Tom and Jerry from Cartoon Network, classic MGM shorts and Popeye from Boomerang, and some episodes of Tom and Jerry Tales from Kids WB. I originally had an episode of She-Ra and an episode of the Super Mario Bros. Super Show on the tape that I recorded from a DVD, but my DVD recorder detected this somehow and edited them out. You might notice the first couple seconds of each. 

A special note:
When I was making these cartoon tapes that I've been uploading lately it was the late 2000s, and I had digital cable and DVR. Hence, I was able to edit, and put things in the order I wanted them in. For most people DVR was a replacement for the VCR, but I realized the full potential of using DVR to make VHS recordings. Most VHS rips you see online are of the "pressed record and left the room for a few hours" variety. Mine are like mixtapes. One might accuse them of being "fake" if they're used to VHS tapes from the 90s, but this is just what's literally on the VHS tapes, copied onto a blank DVD. I honestly don't even know what the point would be of going through the trouble of making a fake video and posting it here. It's not like I'm making money doing this.

You won't see it on this tape in particular, but in the 2010s, I figured out how to run an AV cord from my Playstation 3 to a VCR and record straight from YouTube. This was just for fun really. I would record over stuff on the tapes with YouTube footage, cartoons or things like that. You would probably notice the different aspect ratio on the parts where I did this. Again, not on this particular tape though.

If you're still disappointed in this video or others after my lengthy explanation, I guess I'll have to refund you.

items.title: Down And Dirty Duck (18+) (1974) (WARNING: ADULT CONTENT!)
items.description:
Down and Dirty Duck, promoted under the abbreviated title Dirty Duck, is a 1974 American adult animated comedy film written and directed by Charles Swenson and starring Mark Volman and Howard Kaylan (Flo & Eddie) as the voices of a strait-laced, low-level white-collar worker named Willard and an unnamed duck, among other characters. The plot consists of a series of often abstract sequences, including plot material created by stars Kaylan, Volman, Robert Ridgely, and, according to the film's ending credits, various people Swenson encountered during the making of the film.


Dirty Duck received mostly negative reviews, with many criticizing it for its crude humor and others seeing the film as an attempt to cash in on the success of Ralph Bakshi's Fritz the Cat. The film fared better on home video and is now considered a cult film

WARNING: This animation film was not made for kids, It was made for Adults.

The series focuses on the adventures of two siblings, Emmy and Max, and their dragon friends Ord, Cassie, Zak, Wheezie, and Quetzal. The series began broadcasting on PBS on their newly-renamed PBS Kids block on September 6, 1999, with its final episode airing on November 25, 2005. The show aired reruns up until August 31, 2010, where it was dropped entirely from the PBS Kids lineup. Yearim Productions was responsible for the animation for all seasons ( Sunwoo Entertainment and Wang Film Productions only did animation for season 1), with the exception of Koko Enterprises , which recorded the show along with BLT Productions. items.title: Evolved Virtual Creatures
items.description: This narrated computer animation shows results from a research project involving simulated Darwinian evolutions of virtual block creatures. A population of several hundred creatures is created within a supercomputer, and each creature is tested for their ability to perform a given task, such the ability to swim in a simulated water environment. The successful survive, and their virtual genes containing coded instructions for their growth, are copied, combined, and mutated to make offspring for a new population. The new creatures are again tested, and some may be improvements on their parents. As this cycle of variation and selection continues, creatures with more and more successful behaviors can emerge. The creatures shown are results the final products from many independent simulations in which they were selected for swimming, walking, jumping, following, and competing for control of a green cube.

items.title: Fantasia Special Edition Laserdisc Restoration With Sunflower V 1.0
items.description:
Hello everyone. My username is Class316, and over the years it has bothered me that there was been no authentic version of Fantasia available for viewing (officially or otherwise). Unlike the Original Star Wars Trilogy, Song of the South, and many others, Fantasia never got the same love. So over the years I took it upon myself to find a way to change that.

Ladies and gentlemen, boys and girls, children of all ages, I present to you something that is not only long overdue, but also making its Internet debut! Disney’s timeless classic Fantasia with Fantasound, Deems Taylor’s voice, AND all the censored scenes restored!

As most of you may know, in what is probably one of the earliest cases of cartoon censorship in the name of political correctness, the “offensive” scenes from the Pastoral Symphony of Fantasia were cut out in 1969, never to be seen in official form again. Additionally, Fantasound was lost to time.

In the early 90s Disney would recreate Fantasound theatrically in two theaters, one in New York and one in Los Angeles. This would be dubbed as “Fantasound 90”. And this would be the basis of the audio in the VHS, Laserdisc, and soundtrack CD released in the early 90s. Although a few seconds of audio is missing from the Pastoral Symphony of those releases due to the censorship. Regarding the intros, these home releases use the shortened (and generally more preferred) intros by Deems Taylor.

In 2000, Disney released Fantasia on DVD. This was dubbed “original and uncut” on the cover. Was it uncut? Debatable. It PANNED the “offensive” scenes (thus yielding complete audio at least) but it is anything but “original” as Disney blatantly falsely advertised on the front cover. Additionally, unlike the LD, the DVD audio is far gone from Fantasound. To boot, Disney chose to use the longer intros. In itself perhaps not necessarily a bad thing as some might prefer that. But the audio of said intros were so deteriorated that they couldn’t be used. So rather than work with what was still usable, Disney decided to completely dub Deems Taylor’s voice entirely with that of actor Corey Burton.

Here is a youtube comparison of the uncensored Pastoral Symphony segment compared to the modern-day censored versions: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=gyPFibRadto

In 2010 Fantasia was released on blu ray and its audio was even more far gone from Fantasound than the DVD release (and of course retained the dubbing and censorship of the DVD release).

Another “feature” of both the DVD and blu ray releases is the visual “retouching” that Disney is infamous for when it comes to their older films. Meaning the laserdisc more so reflects the work of the original artists than the more modern releases do.

Now there have been projects on the Internet that have restored all the censored scenes back into Fantasia. But all those releases use the DVD or blu ray release as the basis. Meaning there has yet to be a fully authentic version of Fantasia that is available, officially or otherwise. That is up until February 2021!

Over the years I had collected many Fantasia related things, these include but are not limited to:

In December 2018, I was given (by someone who has long disappeared) a great looking HD version of the censored scenes.

In August 2020, Myspleen.com user AlanGrant released a wonderful rip of the early 90s CAV laserdisc. Here is his write up of it, and I quote:

__start__

This is the 1990 remaster of Fantasia transferred from the CAV LaserDisc boxset, released in January of 1991. This serves not only as a preservation of the 1990 remaster, but of the LaserDisc itself as this is one of numerous disc sets that has disc rot issues which will intensify with time.

Several noticeable differences to other, more modern releases include:

-Color timing is much brighter, especially in the "Nutcracker Suite" section of the film

-A recreation of the 1940 intermission card is used as a title, as opposed to the 1941 "RKO" titlecard used for the 81-minute cut and all post-2000 releases

-Alternate shots with the orchestra in darkness are used for Taylor's narration; later cuts restore Taylor's speaking footage

-Deems Taylor's narration, which was replaced by an actor's redub in post-2000 releases of the film due to deteriorated optical soundtracks

-A ~115 minute runtime made to resemble the 1946 release of the film (which restored Toccata and Fugue), as opposed to the 124-minute 1940 Roadshow version

-An end credits sequence, which all other versions lack

This boxset suffers laser rot to some degree due to the glue used; thankfully here, it's contained to the very beginning of each side. It will be most noticeable in the beginning of the film but each subsequent disc/side has less visual "disc rot".

Transferred using a DVL-90 player, DMR-ES15 passthrough to an AJA Kona LHe card using the S-video input.

Captured as a raw image sequence which was then ran through QTGMC and exported as a 10-bit 4.2.2 H.264 video through ffmpeg (Placebo setting).

(The film runs at 59.94p to better preserve the LaserDisc image as the high framerate and raw modulated image combine to create a "clearer" picture to the eye.)

Digital audio track piped from the DVL-90 to an X-fi Titanium card, bit-matched and recorded as a 44100Hz 16-bit PCM; the file is directly muxed to the .mkv.

Analogue audio was transferred using the AJA KONA LHe card and exported as a monaural Opus file.

Captions were transferred by way of DVD burning on the Panasonic DMR-ES15, ripped using MakeMKV/MKVCleaver and corrected to the .mkv timing in SubtitleEdit.

Chapter stops and titles are direct from the "Chapter Index" insert in the CAV boxset.

__end__

So here I had the most authentic looking and sounding version of Fantasia that Disney put out (ie a HQ LD rip), I had a great looking clip of the censored scenes, among other things.

After many attempts of trying and failing to find someone with the necessary skills and patience to insert the scenes back into the LD and patch up the missing LD audio, on comes user Starbond9 of originaltrilogy.com. I sent him all Fantasia related materials I had collected over the years, and he did a fantastic job. To summarize, he reinserted all the “offensive” scenes into the LD, he patched up the missing audio of the stereo/Fantasound track with that of the DVD audio (the next closest thing we have to Fantasound after the LD), and he patched up the missing audio of the mono track with audio from his own vinyl record!

Here is his write up on what he did, and I quote:

__start__

-Added 5 individual scenes featuring Sunflower and Otica (the centaurette who assists Bacchus)

-Sources on these clips are the audioless HD clips floating around online, color adjusted for LD (adjusted by originaltrilogy.com member BN). The scene with the carpet was from a personal source found on the internet

-3 of said clips were inserted by removing panned/zoomed/and looped existing animations

-2 clips required expanding the video track and inserting a stereo and mono dub as the audio tracks of the movie were physically shortened, see below. (this is also heard on the 1990 CD and Legacy Collection versions of Pastoral)

-Used the DVD stereo audio track as dub source for the missing Fantasound track. These few seconds are NOT Dolby Prologic so listeners with the setting will notice a loss of spatial surround when the two dub spots play. Regular stereo listeners will not notice an issue

-Used a personal copy of a 1961 Mono LP of Pastoral as the dub source for the mono audio track

-Adjusted chapter and subtitles beyond the Pastoral Sunflower clip insert to match the ~8 second shift

-Technical: demuxed individual tracks, remuxed with MKVtoolnix, project assembled in Vegas Pro 14

__end__

I would like to thank him for his time and effort, and for finally bringing an authentic version of Fantasia that showcases, in all its glory, all three of Fantasound, Deems Taylor’s voice, AND the full video/audio of the Pastoral Symphony.

Hopefully someone can also use these two patched up audio tracks for any future Fantasia projects, such as HD 35mm film scans or edits of the blu ray footage.

Please feel free to release this on Torrent, my only request is you keep this write up along with it.

items.title: Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids - The Complete Series
items.description:
In Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids, a young, spirited, obese boy, "Fat Albert Jackson," lives life with his friends, Bill, Russell, Mushmouth, (Ol' Weird) Harold, Bucky, (Dumb) Donald, and Rudy. Together, they love to play games and make music, while learning lessons along the way. Starring Bill Cosby- the "narrator." Every episode-- except for the pilot-- has Bill doing live-action "wraparounds" to guide the audience into the show's lesson. The series is based on his childhood living in North Philadelphia in the 1940's and 50's.

Unfortunately, the same thing that happened with other modern releases of old Filmation cartoons also happened with this series. (Some) DVD releases of the show (especially the 2012 "complete series" one) contained sped-up and high pitched episodes. Every episode has been slowed down 4% and restored to it's correct NTSC speed and pitch. Additionally, I also took the liberty of trying to upscale the audio using a digital audio workstation, because the DVD prints sound horrible. Not every episode sounds perfect, because artifacts and compression are just baked into the masters, but I think I did a pretty good job of making it sound presentable. As for quality, it varies from episode to episode. This cartoon needs a modern-day studio remaster where cels are rescanned, but I think the original source doesn't look too bad. 

It's worth noting that this show went through multiple changes during it's 13-year run:

  • The first four seasons of the show are known as Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids. In these 36 episodes, there's a song at the end (except for two). Ran from 1972-1973 and 1975-1976. During this era, the show covered typical day-to-day problems like meeting new people ("The Stranger"), going to the hospital ("Hospital"), and getting stage fright ("Stage Fright"). However, the series wasn't afraid to cover more serious topics like Marijuana ("Mr. Big Time") and death ("Shuttered Window").
  • Seasons 5-7 were classified as The New Fat Albert Show, featuring the Brown Hornet. Here, the Junkyard Band musical numbers were dropped completely (which was a rather controversial move to many diehard fans), and the show also ramped up a little, covering more serious topics, including child abuse ("Spare the Rod"), gambling ("Heads or Tails?"), and alcohol addiction ("Watch That First Step!"). This "revival" of sorts ran from 1979-1981.
  • Season 8, which premiered in syndication in 1984, is known as The Adventures of Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids. For some reason, Wikipedia says the laugh track and Brown Hornet segments were dropped, but neither is true. The laugh track stays intact, and Brown Hornet appears in multiple episodes. A new segment was added called Legal Eagle. Since this season aired in syndication, it meant they could cover even more serious topics, including prison ("Busted!"), street gangs ("Gang Wars"), and racism ("Long Live the Queen"). Ran from 1984-1985.

FUN FACTS:

  • The writer for the "Junkyard Band" song segments, Ed Fournier, would write all of the season's songs in one day. They were also recorded in the span of one day, with vocals coming from Michael Gray (NOT Bill Cosby)-- who would dub his lines separately. Apparently, one of the musicians said they have tapes of the studio recording the songs, and I would REALLY like to see that one day, because I am super into the Junkyard Band segments (the musician who said that has since passed in early 2022).
  • Despite airing on CBS for over 10 years, Fat Albert and the Cosby Kids moved to NBC in 1989, where it would air reruns, to little fanfare. Reruns also aired on USA Network's Cartoon Express in 1988. Later, in 2011, BOUNCETV would acquire the rights to the cartoon, airing it in primetime and early mornings up until mid-2018, where the show was removed permanently. The show stayed on the schedule despite the Cosby allegations. I included two BOUNCE airings ("Wheeler" and "Faking the Grade") in the collection.
  • A typical episode of the show would cost around $80,000-85,000 to produce, which, adjusted for inflation (2026), would equate to around $600,000-650,000.
  • It would take around four months to produce an episode of Fat Albert, from concept to final production.

ALSO INCLUDED IN THIS COLLECTION:

  • Fat Albert's Easter, Halloween, and Christmas specials.
  • The 1969 pilot ("Hey, Hey, Hey, It's Fat Albert!), and
  • The 1971 pilot ("The Great Go-Cart Race" AKA "The Weird Harold Special"). This special was produced in 1971 but didn't air until 1973-- on NBC, for some reason.
  • The alternate versions of "Shuttered Window" and "Junk Food," featuring the Brown Hornet. Apparently, there are more episodes that have "alternate versions," released on the Time Life video compilations and aired in syndication. I don't own any of the Time Life releases, so you might have to wait a little on that one. I have yet to upload the Brown Hornet segment from "An Ounce of Prevention," but plan to do so in the future.
  • Additionally, there are also allegedly episodes (season 2 ones) that had Bill RE-RECORD his live-action segments in 1984 for the syndication season. Again, haven't come across any of them. Except for the episode "The Newcomer."
  • A 45-minute documentary special, with commentary from Bill Cosby and others on how Fat Albert came to be-- and the impact it had.
  • "Food For Thought," an episode that was meant for schools only, and was never broadcasted on television. This was produced around 1981, so the sixth/seventh season of the show. 
  • The uncensored version of "Busted!" featuring the original dialogue before the episode was edited. This version of the episode contains mild swearing and implied r*pe from the inmates. I can't even believe we have this to begin with, this is insanely rare.
  • The never-before-seen, in-house "Attention Study" versions of the first two episodes of The New Fat Albert Show (but, as you can see if you watch them, the revival was originally titled The New Adventures of Fat Albert) These attention studies were used after the episode had been produced to understand where in the episode the kids' attention spans would drop off for future reference.
  • Shortened versions of episodes, used for schools. These shortened episodes removed the laugh track completely, cut some songs down and removed key scenes to reach the 15-minute mark.

NOTE: For some reason, the laugh track is completely absent on about six episodes. I assume this was just a print/mastering problem, because the laugh track is intact on all of those episodes on the Teletoon Retro encodes, especially of The New Fat Albert Show. The absence of the laugh track causes some pretty awkward silences in-between dialogue, and sometimes, it's just radio silent. So if anyone wants me to replace those with the Teletoon Retro versions that have the laugh tracks, just tell me.

At the end of the day, until we get a streaming/Blu-Ray release (WITH THE CORRECT SPEED), this is the best we have. So cheer on, all you Fat Albert fans, feast to your heart's content. Hey, hey, hey!

items.title: Fleischer Studios' Superman
items.description:
The Fleischer Superman cartoons are a series of seventeen animated short films released in Technicolor by Paramount Pictures and based upon the comic book character Superman, making them his first animated appearance.

They were originally produced by Fleischer Studios, which completed the initial short and eight further cartoons in 1941 and 1942. Production was resumed in May 1942 by Famous Studios, a successor company to Fleischer, which produced eight more cartoons in 1942 and 1943. Superman was the final animated series initiated by Fleischer Studios, before Famous Studios officially took over production.

The first short, "Superman" (1941), alternatively known as "The Mad Scientist" would be nominated for the Academy Award for Best Animated Short of 1941.

All the shorts fell into the public domain when DC Comics (then known as National Comics) failed to renew the copyrights for the shorts.

List of shorts:
Superman (1941) - alternatively known as "The Mad Scientist", Academy Award nominee for Best Animated Short of 1941
The Mechanical Monsters (1941)
Billion Dollar Limited (1942)
The Arctic Giant (1942)
The Bulleteers (1942)
The Magnetic Telescope (1942)
Electric Earthquake (1942)
Volcano (1942)
Terror on the Midway (1942)
Japoteurs (1942)
Showdown (1942)
Eleventh Hour (1942)
Destruction, Inc. (1942)
The Mummy Strikes (1943)
Jungle Drums (1943)
The Underground World (1943)
Secret Agent (1943)

The shorts were originally produced by Fleischer Studios and Famous Studios and were originally distributed by Paramount Pictures, but are all in the public domain, meaning that they are free to use and distribute.

items.title: Flip The Frog - Fiddlesticks
items.description: The following concise, informative description was taken from http://en.wikipedia.org: Flip the Frog was Metro-Goldwyn-Mayer's first sound cartoon. It is about a happy-go-lucky, needy frog, named Flip the Frog. This cartoon was created by Ub Iwerks in 1930. He had drawn a frog and his girlfriend in "Night'", one of the last Silly Symphonies short films he drew while working for Walt Disney. After leaving Disney, Ub Iwerks began the Flip cartoon series with the help of Pat Powers. The first cartoon that Ub Iwerks made for the series was called Fiddlesticks (released on August 16, 1930), and it was also the first color sound cartoon ever made. Fiddlesticks was made in two-color Technicolor. The rest of the Flip series were made in black and white, except for Techno-Cracked (1933). FIDDLESTICKS is perhaps the least funny and entertaining of the FLIP cartoons, many of which have surprisingly adult gags.

This is My Fourth Saturday Morning Recreation I Did For Both YouTube and Archive.org. If You Count the Life With Louie And Ned's Newt Marathon I Made an Few Years Back in February of This Year. So This Saturday Morning Cartoon Recreation Line Up Took So Long. Not Only I Was Busy Try to Finish up So Video Project on My Main YouTube Page But I Was Sick for Two Weeks and Had an Severe Toothache. There a Not People Who makes an Fox Kids Saturday Morning Recreation Specialty From the Year 2000. If it's an Early 2000's Recreation of Fox Kids it Usually 2001 or 2002 but not 2000. That All Going to Change as of Right Now on the Internet. Fox Kids in the Early 2000 Specialty in the Year 2000 was always an Mix Bag For me. I was So Invested in Cartoon Network,Toon Disney and Kids WB that's why Fox Kids as Sort of an Blur for Me and Started to Be the Black Sheep of Cartoon Channel Just like Nickelodeon. Its wasn't as Exciting For me as it was in 1998 and 1999. All My Favorite Show was Cancelled and it last Reruns Since 1999 and it was Going to Be Pile With Action Cartoons,Anime and Worse of All Live Action Shows. Plus The Fox Affiliates Didn't Really Like  Fox Kids and Sold the Rights to 4Kidz Entertainment Until Two Years Later it was Gone. But Fox Kids Did Continue to Air Shows like Digimon,The New Woody Woodpecker Show, Mad Jack the Pirate,Casper,Toonsylvania Life With Louie,Ned's Newt and Many Others that Stared or Got Cancelled in the Late 90's and aired More Time Until One Year After.The Donkey Kong Cartoon was Still Airing to Capitalize on DK64 and DKC Gameboy Color success. And We Did Some Underrated Cartoons and Animes like MedaBots,Mon Colle Knights,Angela Anaconda,Action Man,The Vision of Escaflowne and DinoZaurs That Aired on the Network that I Remember. Also the Mega Man and Dungeons and Dragons Cartoon was Re-airing Again on TV Since 1985 and 1996 prosperity. Mega man Cartoon was on a Block Called Anime Invasion That Combine all the Anime and some Action Cartoons that as Inspired By Anime on the Block and the Dungeons and Dragons Cartoon  aired on Fox Kids to Capitalize on the Hype For the Dungoens and Dragons Live Action Movie was as Airing at the Time. Powers Ranger Re-Runs Was Still Airing For old Fans and New PR Show was Coming out. Also Fox Kids Gave as an Awesome Behind The Scenes Look on Don Bluth's Newest Action Cartoon Sci-Fi Film Titan A.E.  (Underrated Master Piece If I Do Say so My Self.)
Some Cartoons and Live Action Shows Had to Be Alter due to Some Copyrights. Also I add the Show the PJ's to My Saturday Morning Cartoon Recreation Line Up. Even Though it Didn't Air on Fox Kids Block  Just The Regular Fox Network. I Wanted to fill in the Gap for Cartoon Comedy Base Shows.

items.title: Freakazoid! Complete Season 1-2 (1995-1997)
items.description: Freakazoid! is an American superhero comedy animated television series created by Bruce Timm and Paul Dini and developed by Tom Ruegger for the Kids' WB programming block of The WB. The series chronicles the adventures of the title character, Freakazoid, a crazy teenage superhero who battles with a bizarre array of supervillains. The show also features mini-episodes of adventures of other bizarre superheroes. The show was produced by Amblin Entertainment and Warner Bros. Animation. The cartoon was the third animated series produced by the collaboration of Steven Spielberg and Warner Bros. Animation during the animation renaissance of the 1990s. Bruce Timm, best known as a major principal of the DC Animated Universe, originally intended it to be a straightforward superhero action-adventure cartoon with comic overtones, but executive producer Steven Spielberg asked series producer and writer Tom Ruegger and the Animaniacs team to turn Freakazoid! into a flat-out comedy. The show is similar to fellow Ruegger-led programs such as Animaniacs, and the humor is unique in its inclusions of slapstick, fourth wall firings, parody, surreal humor and pop cultural references. Much to my delight: I stumbled upon the trainwreck, of the corpses, of three DVDs. The archivist that uploaded them has a very unusual method of disassembling multiple DVDs and stacking the like pieces from all of them together in different heaps … I assure you that this jumbles them up very thoroughly. I was only delighted because I had just figured out a method, to finally recover the master videos, from another series of eight DVDs - that were also very completely jumbled up by the same person.

I got this series of 52 videos out of that last batch of Scrambled Up DVDs: https://archive.org/details/shadow-raiders That DVD set had two different languages: and I got both recovered.

I just found the old 1969 TV Series H. R. Pufnstuff … all thoroughly mixed together (like I said: it is a trainwreck). But now I'm getting better at recovery, from this archivist's … rather unique … way of backing up DVDs - not as ISO Images but as Stacks of Files (all named the same), - and I turned the unwatchable mess on the source page of https://archive.org/details/h.r.-pufnstuf into this page - with a complete TV series: ready for you to enjoy.

This DVD set has no subtitles or alternate languages - just 17 episodes of nostalgic goodness (or pure camp: from a bygone era) … and an unexpected find of a H. R. Pufnstuf picture, and coloring, and song book: with the sheet music AND lyrics to Twelve of the original Songs of the TV series (perhaps written by Sid and Marty Krofft themselves?) - you could play and/or sing along!!! 
It says on the Cover: "Three books in one … Coloring Book / Photo Book / Song Book.   West Coast Publications, INC.  Star Series 29  $2.95" (That was in 1969 Dollars)
Videos … with Song Sheet Music on the Same Page - to a few of the songs in the videos: this is the Only One in my Video Collection! 
https://archive.org/download/h_r_pufnstuf/pufnstuf_coloring_song_book.pdf

I got a copy of "The Pufnstuf Movie" from this page: https://archive.org/details/H.R.Pufnstuf and if you want to see more Pufnstuf, or Jack Wild (Oliver!), videos: you need to go check that huge collection out!!! Many many more hours of great videos!!

I also found (on YouTube), and posted, a Lo-Rez copy of the Satire done about the show - but please do not watch that last forbidden video. It will rot your mind. And it is a popular lie: " … I can't speak to what adults were doing when they were watching the shows. We just set out to make a quality children's program". Sadly, Marty Krofft DID Not create under the influence (Sid … who knows?). It's just a kid's puppet show: gone rogue.

These videos actually have historic, as well as entertainment, value. Think about it: nothing from the 1970's - or Later - can be seen in here. 
This is a video Time Capsule of 1969 … how it looked then / how it sounded / how they did things fifty five years ago. And at least one review posted testifies to the lifelong joy and inspiration given by the Krofft Brothers to a generation of kids - they DID Change lives! What a legacy to leave behind!

I found a video right here on the Archive about the career and lives of Sid and Marty Krofft and it's pretty good! If you like this series and want to learn more about how it came about / how it was made / and insider details about it, go watch:

(The NOTES look like "ALL b's, O's, and d's"!! Are you SURE this is in English?!?)  I tried reading it's output text / spasm: and laughed for several minutes!!! "Tease a Computer" and this brilliant alphanumeric salad is about what you should expect!!!
